people living with cancer would prefer to have a primary care team who: • have a holistic approach to the care of people living with cancer • are aware of the impact of cancer on the whole family • are able to communicate with the patient, carer and family • are able, where possible, to provide continuity of care • have access to the patient’s records • can offer support for the patient, carers and family • are aware of and able to access the range of services available to the person
the patient's wishes and preferences for care are paramount, and that patients and carers are the best judges of the quality of the care that they receive.
the patients with cancer and carers in our study wished for a more holistic and person-centred approach to care, with the primary care team taking a more proactive role in their management and care.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients and their carers want to be cared for by their GP, but not just in a traditional sense.
patients want to be treated as people first, and patients with cancer second.
patients and carers with cancer would like to receive a more holistic approach to their care, and that they want more information, more support, and a more flexible and individualised approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patients and carers have very clear ideas about what they would like to be offered by primary care.
patients with cancer want to be cared for at home by their GP, and to be involved in decisions about their care.
people with cancer want a primary care service that is flexible to meet their needs and that they are not afraid to ask for what they want.
